- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong downward spikes (sentiment < 0.4) — adjust downward bias to avoid overcorrection.
- Overshoot after recent price spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below prior high if sentiment is neutral or cooling.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show rising prices with sentiment > 0.7, reduce forecast slope to avoid overbought overcorrection.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops sharply 2–3 days before forecast peak, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to account for delayed market reaction.
- Avoid overconfidence in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — reduce forecast magnitude if sentiment is volatile or low.
